candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated user with WRITE access to a bucket can POST a crafted multipart extension bundle to /buckets/{bucketId}/bundles/{bundleType}. The NAR main manifest controls Nar-Group, Nar-Id, and Nar-Version. Values such as '..' pass BundleIdentifier.validateNotBlank and are persisted as the bundle's group/artifact/version; FileUtils.sanitizeFilename replaces slash, backslash, colon, NUL, and control characters, but leaves '..' unchanged.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked the upload and manifest parsers: group/artifact/version are not restricted to UUID/Maven/path-safe patterns and only need to be non-blank. Checked the sanitizer: it replaces path separators and other invalid characters, but explicitly does not reject '.' or '..'. Checked the provider: path construction uses new File(...), with no normalize(), canonical-path, startsWith(), or real-path containment check. Checked shipped configuration: the filesystem bundle provider is the default. Impact qualifications: the final filename has a provider-appended .nar or .cpp suffix and the deletion behavior requires a subsequent authorized deletion or administrative cleanup; those conditions are reflected above rather than claimed as unconditional.
candidates.impact: A crafted bundle can cause directory creation and attacker-controlled NAR/CPP bytes to be written outside the configured extension-bundle storage directory, potentially overwriting an existing matching .nar/.cpp file. If the crafted bundle or its bucket is deleted, cleanDirectory() can recursively delete the registry data, configuration, and application files under the parent of the default ./extension_bundles directory. Consequences range from registry data loss/denial of service to possible code execution if an overwritten or planted archive is later loaded, although that final execution step was not verified.
candidates.prerequisites: The default FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider must be active (it is the shipped providers.xml default), and the attacker needs bucket WRITE permission to upload the crafted bundle. Triggering the destructive cleanDirectory path additionally requires DELETE permission for the bundle/bucket, or a later administrator cleanup that deletes the crafted bundle or its bucket. The uploaded file must be parseable as the selected bundle type, with a main manifest and any required extension metadata.
candidates.root_cause: NAR manifest groupId, artifactId, and version values are accepted with only a non-blank check. FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider sanitizes filesystem-reserved characters but does not reject the path components '.' or '..', does not normalize the resulting path, and does not verify containment under bundleStorageDir. saveOrUpdateBundleVersion can therefore write outside the configured root, and deleteAllBundleVersions later passes an escaping path to Apache Commons cleanDirectory().
candidates.title: Extension bundle coordinates allow filesystem path traversal and recursive deletion outside the configured bundle-storage root
candidates.trace: BucketBundleResource.createExtensionBundleVersion -> StandardExtensionService.createBundleVersion -> NarBundleExtractor.getBundleCoordinate -> BundleIdentifier accepts non-blank '..' -> StandardExtensionService.persistBundleVersionContent -> FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider.getBundleVersionDirectory builds new File(bundleStorageDir, bucketId + '/' + groupId + '/' + artifactId + '/' + version). With groupId='..', artifactId='..', and version='evil', this resolves to the parent of extension_bundles and creates/writes there. Separately, StandardExtensionService.deleteBundle builds a BundleCoordinate from the stored malicious values; FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider.deleteAllBundleVersions calls getBundleDirectory (bucketId/group/artifact) and then cleanDirectory() on the resolved path. With groupId and artifactId both '..', the path resolves to bundleStorageDir's parent, so all entries under that parent can be recursively deleted.
candidates.unverified: No code, tests, or HTTP requests were executed. The exact behavior of the bundled servlet container and deployed permissions, the ability to complete a crafted NAR upload, and whether any out-of-root archive would later be loaded are not runtime-confirmed. The primary path traversal and cleanDirectory sink are directly evident in source.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

coverage_summary: Source scope reported 7,359 root files and 7,332 model-visible files, with 27 sensitive-name/path exclusions and no symlinks; read_file/search_code enforce a per-file text limit. The P1 relation scope was partial: 7,091 files indexed, 268 source files missing from the index, 248 omitted, 3 parse errors, no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution, and 152,836 unresolved calls. I performed broad targeted source searches across Java for process execution, deserialization, XML/YAML parsing, SQL construction, filesystem/path APIs, authentication, CSRF, JWT, and Registry persistence, then manually traced the Registry upload, NAR extraction, bundle persistence, download, and deletion paths. Coverage is not exhaustive over every source file or dependency.
limitations: No build, tests, runtime, HTTP, or exploit execution was performed; findings are source-evidence leads only.
The P1 index omits many files and provides only syntax/navigation relations, so absence of an index relation does not establish absence of reachability or data flow.
The destructive delete path depends on DELETE authorization or an administrator later deleting the crafted bundle/bucket.
Potential code execution from an out-of-root NAR was not verified; only the path traversal and file-system write/delete behavior are source-supported.
Dependency-level vulnerabilities and deployment-specific provider/authorization configurations were not independently validated.

rejected_leads.lead: Client-side path traversal in ClientUtils.getExtensionBundleVersionContent, where a Content-Disposition filename is parsed and passed to Files.copy(new File(outputDirectory, filename)).
rejected_leads.reason: This is a plausible separate client-side sink, but the filename origin and the CLI/API route needed to exercise slash-containing bundle coordinates were not fully traced. It was not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Client-supplied VersionedFlow.identifier is retained by StandardServiceFacade.createFlow and later used by FileSystemFlowPersistenceProvider as a directory component.
rejected_leads.reason: The source is suspicious, but creating and applying a snapshot with a slash-containing flow ID requires the flowId in the HTTP route to match the body identifier; servlet path normalization and encoded-slash handling were not verified.

rejected_leads.lead: OIDCAccessResource.checkOidcState forwards an error page on a bad state but does not abort the callback, allowing subsequent code exchange to continue.
rejected_leads.reason: This appears to weaken login CSRF protection, but response commitment and practical exploitability were not established; it was not selected.

summary: Selected one source-supported candidate: path traversal through unvalidated extension-bundle coordinates in NiFi Registry's default filesystem extension-bundle provider. Crafted NAR manifest values are only required to be non-blank, survive filename sanitization as '.'/'..', and are used directly as filesystem path components. This permits writes outside the configured bundle-storage root and, when the crafted bundle is later deleted, recursive deletion of the storage root's parent. No additional candidates are submitted.
